record.paper_title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems
record.original_question: For the copolymer model with α = 1/2, prove that the weak-coupling critical slope m_{1/2} is strictly larger than 2/3.

evidence.quote: here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the disordered copolymer model defined as follows. Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting at $0$, with law $\mathbf{P}$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, with law $\mathbb{P}$. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (coupling intensity) and $h\ge 0$ (asymmetry bias), and for $N\in\mathbb{N}$, define the polymer measure of length $N$ by
$$\frac{d\mathbf{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{d\mathbf{P}}(S) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\,\exp\!\Big(\lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\Big),$$
with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(0)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$, and where $Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. The quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}$$
exists and is non-negative; the localized phase is $\{\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)>0\}$ and the delocalized phase is $\{\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=0\}$. There is a critical curve $h_c:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ separating these phases, and it is known that the limit
$$m \;=\; \lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0} \frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}$$
exists in $(0,1]$. (More generally, when the underlying random-walk return-time distribution has tails of index $1+\alpha$ with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the corresponding weak-coupling slope is denoted $m_\alpha$, and the simple random walk corresponds to $\alpha=1/2$.)

It is known that $m_\alpha\ge 1/(1+\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$; in particular $m_{1/2}\ge 2/3$.

Prove that
$$m_{1/2} \;>\; \tfrac{2}{3}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The strict inequality $m_\alpha > 1/(1+\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ was established by Bolthausen, den Hollander, and Opoku, ruling out Monthus' conjecture $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$. In particular this gives $m_{1/2}>2/3$, resolving the problem (although the exact value of $m_{1/2}$ remains unknown).

status_evidence.title: The Critical Curves of the Random Pinning and Copolymer Models at Weak Coupling
status_evidence.snippet: Bolthausen, den Hollander and Opoku showed this lower bound is strict for every α ∈ (0,∞), thus ruling out Monthus' conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: It has been proven that m_alpha > 1/(1+alpha) for every alpha in (0,infty), so in particular m_{1/2} > 2/3.
